messages:
mira: quick heads-up — postdeploy quick-smoke for v0.23.1 canary (5%) showing KV probe p95 uplift in eu1. attaching initial summary.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: v0.23.1 -> canary=5% (hosts: canary-eu1-03..05) :rocket:
tom: confirming, p95 for kvprobe jumped 130ms -> ~420ms at 12:07UTC. small sample but consistent across three canary hosts.
carla: saw same in synth logs, retries are happening after 250ms window. snippet from synth-agent:
```
[2026-03-21T12:07:15Z] kvprobe: request id=abcd retry=1 latency=395ms status=200
[2026-03-21T12:07:16Z] kvprobe: request id=efgh latency=412ms status=200
```

carla: looks like backend acks are delayed, not 5xxs.

infra-oncall: I'm checking infra metrics. node-level IO and CPU look fine; noticing a small threadpool saturation on canary instances. pulling logs now.

ben: can we run a one-off manual probe against a canary host to reproduce? curl example:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://canary-eu1-03.internal/kvprobe -d '{"key":"smoke-123"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE_TOKEN' -w '\\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code} TIME:%{time_total}'
```

ben: ran that 10x — 3/10 above 300ms.
mira: given this, proposal: pause ramp (stop further rollout), reduce canary to 0% (rollback canary), or pin traffic to v0.23.0 for the moment while we triage. Thoughts?
tom: +1 to pause. not confident to rollback entire release yet — it's specific to kvprobe tail. maybe scale canary hosts down/up to see if transient.
carla: if we pin to 0.23.0 we avoid customer impact. but if root cause is infra (threadpool), restarting pods might clear it without full rollback.
infra-oncall: I can roll restart canary pods sequentially now (graceful). ETA 6m for first rotation.
qa-bot: quick synthetic run pre/post restart: pre-restart p95=410ms, pre-restart error=0. post-restart will report.
deploy-bot: Canary ramp paused per request by mira. No further traffic increases will occur.
infra-oncall: restarted canary-eu1-03 and canary-eu1-04. monitoring.
qa-bot: post-restart sample: p95=145ms, 10/10 responses <200ms. looks improved on restarted hosts.
ben: can confirm canary-eu1-05 (not restarted) still showing ~380ms p95.
mira: consensus: hold rollout, pin active traffic back to v0.23.0, and keep canary at 0% until we validate restarts on all canary hosts. create follow-up ticket INF-1234 to root-cause threadpool/retry behavior.
carla: filing a brief postmortem note and adding probe traces to INF-1234.
deploy-bot: Traffic pinned to v0.23.0 as of 12:28UTC. Canary=0%.
mira: thanks — if canary restarts fix remaining hosts we can do a controlled reattempt with extra telemetry. For now we hold and will update this thread when INF-1234 has initial triage.
ben: noting action items: (1) finish restarts (infra), (2) full canary probe sweep (qa), (3) trace+heap dump capture if saturation recurs (carla/infra).
